text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, learning patterns and relationships between words through this vast training data. When you give a model a prompt, it uses these patterns to generate a response. Prompt engineering, or the skill of writing clear and specific instructions, is crucial because well-designed prompts lead to more useful outputs. These models can summarize documents, translate languages, and even write code. However, they have clear limits. They don't truly understand information and can confidently produce false or biased statements, so it's important to check their answers carefully.
